senses.definition: To reword a draft so it reads better without changing what it says.
senses.caution: It is fine about your own draft. Calling someone else's change 'just wordsmithing' dismisses it as cosmetic, which is unfair if their point was real.
senses.example: The recommendation is agreed. Give me an hour to wordsmith it before it goes to the committee.

cues.text: Your manager has approved what the memo argues but the sentences are clumsy. You want to offer to fix how it reads without reopening the argument.
In a review, a colleague keeps proposing small changes to how a paragraph reads while the actual decision is still unresolved, and you want a name for what the meeting has turned into.
You are helping a friend tighten a wedding speech. The content is entirely theirs and you are only working on how each line lands.
You have drafted a difficult message to a family member and want to spend twenty minutes on exactly how each sentence reads before you send it.

distractors: To make something deliberately hard to understand.
To make a bad situation worse than it already was.
To turn a structure held in memory into a form that can be stored or sent.
To use your own product for real work before you ask anyone else to use it.
To speak about someone in a way that quietly lowers them.
